chapters.intro: The words and phrases you need at the doctor, the pharmacy, the dentist and the hospital. Tap 🔊 to hear each Dutch phrase spoken.

sections.title: Waar ga je heen?
sections.note: The places and people in Dutch health care.

sections.title: Start with the huisarts
sections.body: Your huisarts (GP) is always your first contact for medical problems. If you need a specialist or a hospital, the huisarts gives you a verwijzing (referral) first. For urgent problems in the evening, at night or in the weekend, when your own practice is closed, you call the huisartsenpost. In a life-threatening emergency, do not wait: bel 112.

sections.title: Klachten & symptomen
sections.note: How to say what is wrong with you.

sections.title: Bij de apotheek
sections.note: At the pharmacy, where you collect medicine. Read the instructions carefully.

sections.title: Bij de tandarts
sections.note: At the dentist. Go for a check-up about twice a year.

sections.title: Mental health matters too
sections.body: Health is not only about your body. If you feel down, anxious or stressed for a long time, you can talk about it with your huisarts. The huisarts listens and can give you a verwijzing to the GGZ (geestelijke gezondheidszorg, mental health care) or to a psycholoog. Asking for help is normal and the conversation is confidential.

sections.title: Handige zinnen
sections.note: Full sentences you can use right away.

items.en: I would like to make an appointment.
I have had a fever since yesterday.

sections.q: U bent ziek. Wie belt u eerst?
sections.qEn: You are ill. Who do you contact first?
sections.explanation: In the Netherlands the huisarts (GP) is always your first contact. The huisarts treats you or, if needed, gives a verwijzing (referral) to a specialist or the hospital. You do not go straight to a specialist or the hospital yourself.
